# Per-node environment exposure, bounded by an operator allowlist

A node declares which environment variables its agent may read. The operator
declares which variables any node may ask for. The agent gets the intersection.

## The template

Three agent nodes, each declaring a different single variable.

```yaml
name: expose-env-demo
version: "1"
nodes:
  - type: alpha
    executor: claude-agent
    attributes:
      schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          model:         {type: string, default: "claude-sonnet-4-5"}
          system_prompt: {type: string, default: "per-node expose-env"}
          user_prompt:   {type: string, default: "..."}
          cli:
            type: object
            default:
              expose_env: [VALIDATOR_TOKEN]

  - type: beta
    executor: claude-agent
    attributes:
      schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          model:         {type: string, default: "claude-sonnet-4-5"}
          system_prompt: {type: string, default: "per-node expose-env"}
          user_prompt:   {type: string, default: "..."}
          cli:
            type: object
            default:
              expose_env: [REVIEWER_SEED]

  - type: gamma
    executor: claude-agent
    attributes:
      schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          model:         {type: string, default: "claude-sonnet-4-5"}
          system_prompt: {type: string, default: "per-node expose-env"}
          user_prompt:   {type: string, default: "..."}
          cli:
            type: object
            default:
              expose_env: [OPERATOR_ONLY_SECRET]
```

## With an operator allowlist in force

```bash
docker run -d -p 8080:8080 \
  -e CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN=... \
  -e RIMSKY_CLAUDE_AGENT_EXPOSE_ENV_ALLOWLIST=VALIDATOR_TOKEN,REVIEWER_SEED \
  -e VALIDATOR_TOKEN=... -e REVIEWER_SEED=... -e OPERATOR_ONLY_SECRET=... \
  rimsky-all-in-one:<tag>
```

`alpha`'s agent reads exactly `VALIDATOR_TOKEN`, at the operator-set value.
`beta`'s agent reads exactly `REVIEWER_SEED`. Neither reads the other's
variable, even though both values are present in the container.

`gamma` declares a variable outside the allowlist. Its dispatch fails with
`agent/attribute_invalid`, and the error payload names the variable
(`disallowed_env_var: OPERATOR_ONLY_SECRET`), the instance, the node, and the
allowlist variable `RIMSKY_CLAUDE_AGENT_EXPOSE_ENV_ALLOWLIST`.

A node gets a variable only if it declared it and the operator permitted it.

## With no operator allowlist

Run the same template with `RIMSKY_CLAUDE_AGENT_EXPOSE_ENV_ALLOWLIST` unset.

`gamma` now reads the variable it declares. `alpha` and `beta` still read only
their own declarations. An unset allowlist widens the operator's boundary; it
does not dissolve the author's.

## Exposed values do not land in persisted state

Read the deployment's own history back after the run:

```bash
curl -sS "$BASE/v1/observability/events?instance_id=$IID&limit=500"
curl -sS "$BASE/v1/observability/node-runs?instance_id=$IID&limit=200"
curl -sS "$BASE/v1/instances/$IID"
curl -sS "$BASE/v1/audit?limit=500"
curl -sS "$BASE/v1/nodes/$NODE_ID"
```

None of the exposed plaintext values appears in any of those five surfaces.
Exposing a credential to one agent node does not write that credential into the
deployment's history, where it would outlive the dispatch and be readable by
anyone who can read the instance.

What an agent does with a value once it has it belongs to that agent.
